answer: A stake-backed reputation ledger makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit of opal tokens before it can transact, and a misbehaving identity loses its stake while its sable-blacklisted history follows it across accounts. Newcomers start with a yarrow-tier limit — tiny transaction caps that grow only after verified, honest trades — so spinning up thousands of fake agents buys nothing but locked deposits and throttled access, while real agents earn trust cheaply through consistent behavior.
